audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart calls Level 1, Levels 4-5 and Level 6 'Skill' and gives 2+ items to Renekton, while the packet chart and the page's own whys say Renekton owns levels 1-6 and Yasuo takes over with items.
audit.why: 48.74% over 3055 games with the packet chart reading Renekton x6 then Yasuo; the mirror audit (renekton__yasuo) already aligned its side to the same chart, so leaving these rows would put the two pages in direct contradiction.
audit.corrected: Levels 1, 4-5 and 6 to Renekton; 2+ items to Yasuo. Four matched side/win pairs, proposed as one atomic group.

audit.why: Spikes are placed correctly: Renekton at 3 with fury, Dominus at 6 (120/100/80s), Yasuo needing two crit items before the pattern overtakes him.
audit.corrected: Kept the spike timings; only the Wind Wall claims inside spikes[1] and spikes[3] were repaired.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places tell you to Wind Wall Renekton — 'Save Wind Wall for Ruthless Predator (W) stun', 'wall the W stun and back off', 'Wind Wall his gap-close autos'. Renekton casts no projectiles and his autos are melee, so Wind Wall blocks none of it.
audit.why: Yasuo's W text is explicit: it blocks enemy PROJECTILES for 4 seconds. Renekton's Q (325 range melee sweep), W (300 range melee slashes) and E (450 dash) are all non-projectile. The only real use of the wall here is its terrain body: it stops the Slice and Dice dash path.
audit.corrected: Wall is terrain, not a stun answer — body-block Slice and Dice with it. Also added the two missing interactions: his empowered Cull the Meek heals him back so Executioner's Calling decides long trades, and Ruthless Predator is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up animation is your cue to step out, not the cast.

audit.why: Ruthless Predator is correctly identified as the punishable cooldown; rank 1 is 16s, dropping to 8s at rank 5, and Slice and Dice is 16s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Used the 8s W figure in the late-game text so the kiting advice is concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] was flagged as a wrong ability name.
audit.why: FALSE POSITIVE — Slice and Dice is Renekton's real E name per the kit. The genuine weakness was that the line gave no timing.
audit.corrected: Rewrote it around the 16s rank-1 E cooldown rather than renaming anything.

edits.after: Use Wind Wall as terrain to body-block Slice and Dice, not his W

edits.after: His Dominus (R) gives him a huge health bar and AoE damage on demand; his all-in windows are already strong, so 6 only widens his lead — don't contest a fury-loaded fight; Wind Wall cannot stop his W.

edits.before: Renekton falls off as a lane bully and you scale past him: at 100% crit you Wind Wall his gap-close autos, kite the stun, and finally out-DPS his short combo window.
edits.after: Renekton falls off as a lane bully and you scale past him: at 100% crit you stay outside his 325-range Q, kite the 8s W stun, and finally out-DPS his short combo window.

edits.before: Renekton is a lane bully who scales poorly; once you hit two crit items you Wind Wall his engage autos, kite the W-stun, and out-DPS his brief combo, taking clear control of the matchup.
edits.after: Renekton is a lane bully who scales poorly; once you hit two crit items you sidestep Slice and Dice, kite the 8s W-stun on E dashes, and out-DPS his brief combo, taking clear control of the lane.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: W is an auto-attack reset — back off on his wind-up, not on the cast.

edits.before: That is Renekton's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Empowered Cull the Meek heals him back — buy Executioner's Calling before you trade long.

notes: The packet suspectName on wants.foe[1] is a FALSE POSITIVE: Slice and Dice is the correct E name. The real defect was three separate lines telling the player to Wind Wall a champion who casts zero projectiles — Renekton's Q, W and E are all melee or dash. Level-chart edits are one atomic group of four matched side/win pairs, all four moving the page onto the packet chart and onto the already-audited mirror. The chart's whys already described Renekton winning those stages, so only the tokens were wrong.
